description:
MEASURED 2026-09-11, examples/epithermal_slowing_down.rs.

DEFECT. The collision kernel has exactly two scattering branches (keff_delta.rs:865, keff.rs:1329/1456/1576, transport_csg.rs:817):

  if let Some((e_out, mu_lab)) = nuc.sample_thermal(e, seed) { .. }   // S(a,b) only
  else { two_body_scatter_with_mu(..) / elastic_scatter(..) }          // TARGET AT REST

There is no free-gas target-velocity sampling anywhere in the crate (grep: no maxwell/target_vel/sample_target outside the fission-spectrum samplers). So any nuclide WITHOUT a thermal table — in the FHR pebble that is Li-7, Be-9, F-19 (the whole FLiBe coolant), O-16 and the free-gas C of the UCO kernel, and Si/C of the SiC coating — scatters off a stationary nucleus at ALL energies, thermal included. Outgoing energy is confined to [alpha*E, E]: it can only go DOWN. There is no up-scatter, so there is no thermal equilibrium.

OpenMC samples the target velocity below FREE_GAS_THRESHOLD = 400 kT (sample_target_velocity, src/physics.cpp). At 600 K that is E < 20.7 eV — i.e. the entire thermal range AND the 6.674 eV / 20.87 eV U-238 resonances.

MEASUREMENT (20000 walkers x 400 scatters from 1 eV, 600 K; a free gas must relax to <E> = 1.5 kT = 0.0776 eV):

  medium                      <E> final [eV]   <E>/1.5kT
  C12 (graphite S(a,b))            1.0037e-1     1.29e0     <- correct, has the TSL
  C12 (free gas, kernel C)         1.4810e-27    1.91e-26
  Be9  (FLiBe)                     1.7868e-35    2.30e-34
  F19  (FLiBe)                     3.2696e-18    4.22e-17
  Li7  (FLiBe)                     7.2250e-44    9.32e-43
  O16  (UCO kernel)                2.8223e-21    3.64e-20
  Si28 (SiC coating)               8.2994e-13    1.07e-11
  U238 (heavy control)             3.4202e-2     4.41e-1    <- xi tiny, still falling

Every non-TSL medium cools without bound. The per-collision kinematics are correct (xi/xi_0 = 1.000 from 4 eV to 10 keV, no kinematic-floor violations); the defect is the ABSENCE OF A FIXED POINT, which no per-collision check can see.

WHY THIS IS THE RING-RPT LEAD (op-mzvp.2.12). It is the only surviving mechanism that fits every constraint:
 - right sign for all three symptoms: an over-cooled spectrum depletes the 0.1-6 eV tail, so U-238 resonance capture is under-counted (p too HIGH), non-thermal production falls (eps too LOW), and k comes out HIGH;
 - invisible to every sigma oracle (point sigma vs NJOY PENDF +-0.04%, capture RESONANCE INTEGRAL vs NJOY and vs published RI_inf +0.00%, graphite vs THERMR +-0.05%);
 - invisible to the earlier xi check, which measured ONLY graphite and ONLY below 3.9 eV — i.e. only the one nuclide that HAS a thermal table;
 - shared by both pebbles (a kernel property, not a geometry one), as op-mzvp.2.8 requires;
 - absent from Godiva, which is why the HIGH data path reproduces ICSBEP HEU-MET-FAST-001 to +57 +- 173 pcm (examples/godiva_keff_endf_local.rs) while the pebble misses by +1700.

FIX: port OpenMC sample_target_velocity (constant-cross-section / Cullen rejection scheme) and do the collision in the moving-target CM frame, gated at E < 400 kT with awr > 1. Wire into all five collision sites. Then re-run examples/fhr_ring_rpt_endf.rs and record the delta-k.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
FIXED and MEASURED 2026-09-11.

IMPLEMENTATION: physics::scatter::free_gas_elastic_scatter + sample_target_velocity, a port of OpenMC src/physics.cpp in the constant-cross-section (CXS) approximation, gated at FREE_GAS_THRESHOLD = 400 kT with awr > 1 (above which it delegates to the target-at-rest form bit-for-bit). Wired into all five collision sites: keff_delta.rs, keff.rs x3 (collide_batched, transport_history, transport_history_tabulated), transport_csg.rs.

ORACLE. Two oracles were tried first and BOTH WERE WRONG; recording them so nobody re-derives them:
 - <dE> = 2A/(1+A)^2 * (2kT - E). Gets both limits right (target-at-rest loss at high E, the 2kT fixed point) and misses the collision-rate |v_rel| weighting in between. Off by 5.3% at A=2.
 - the chain's stationary law is Gamma(2,kT). Same flaw: the collision rate goes as the mean RELATIVE speed, not the neutron speed. Off by 3.9% (mean) / 4.6% (second moment) at A=2, and far less at A=238 -- the signature of exactly that term.
The oracle that IS exact: the equilibrium neutron DENSITY must be Maxwellian. Weight the chain's own samples by 1/v_rel_bar(E), v_rel_bar = sqrt(E)*[(1+1/(2a^2))erf(a) + exp(-a^2)/(a*sqrt(pi))], a = sqrt(A E/kT); then <E> = 1.5 kT and <E^2> = 3.75 (kT)^2. Holds for A = 2, 8.9, 11.9, 15.9, 236 (free_gas_equilibrium_density_is_maxwellian). Plus: bit-identical to target-at-rest above 400 kT, asymptotic first moment at 300 kT, up-scatter permitted at 0.0253 eV, 2kT random-walk fixed point.

EFFECT ON THE RING-RPT CASE (same deck, same seeds, same settings):
  sphere            before -> after        delta
  explicit TRISO    1.38191 -> 1.39610    +1419 pcm
  ring-RPT          1.38354 -> 1.40739    +2385 pcm
  naive homog       1.35656 -> 1.37323    +1667 pcm
  ring-RPT (CSG)    1.38279 -> 1.40757    +2478 pcm

Six factors vs OpenMC's ring-RPT reference:
  eta 2.0155 -> 2.0096 (ref 2.0073): error 0.41% -> 0.11%
  f   0.9140 -> 0.9199 (ref 0.9216): error 0.83% -> 0.18%
  p   0.5266 -> 0.5368 (ref 0.4842): error +8.8% -> +10.9%
  eps 1.4131 -> 1.3976 (ref 1.5043): error -6.1% -> -7.1%

THE PREDICTED SIGN IN THIS BEAD WAS WRONG. I wrote 'right sign for all three symptoms'. It is the right sign for eta and f -- they snapped onto the reference, which is what a thermal-kernel defect should own -- and the WRONG sign for k: the disagreement with OpenMC GREW, from +1681 to +3100 pcm on the explicit pebble. A correct fix moving the answer away from the reference means the earlier agreement was partly cancellation and the remaining error is larger than it looked. Recorded as the result; not reverted.

The residual is now ENTIRELY p*eps: ours 0.5368*1.3976 = 0.7502, OpenMC 0.4842*1.5043 = 0.7284, +3.00%, against a k ratio of +3.13%. Same number. Handing back to op-mzvp.2.12 with that localisation.

FALLOUT. tests/htr10_graphite_thermal_scattering_pebble_bed.rs asserted bound-graphite vs 'free-gas' separate by >=5 sigma, and recorded free-gas k = 1.08838 vs bound 1.95254 (37 sigma) on 2026-08-14 -- with an interpretation that named this exact defect ('stationary-target, no up-scatter') without recognising it as a bug. That 0.86 delta-k was the size of the bug. Re-measured at 18x statistics against a CORRECT free gas: 1.93656 +- 0.00316 vs 1.94020 +- 0.00361, i.e. +364 +- 479 pcm (0.76 sigma), consistent with zero. The test now asserts the AGREEMENT (which catches a regression to target-at-rest at 37 sigma) and liveness moved to a new test that probes the collision loop's own branch: <E'/E> at 0.0253 eV, free gas 1.13863 +- 0.00123 vs bound 1.03858 +- 0.00062, 72 sigma. This also retires the '~1700 pcm for graphite S(a,b)' figure the ring-RPT V&V doc cited from that test.

title: outram-mc: no free-gas target motion — every nuclide without S(a,b) scatters off a target AT REST at all energies

description:

physics/column_config.rs: the default 8-stage benzene/toluene plant config, built the same way op-6rhz's V&V test builds it (RigorousColumn::distillation(...).solver_input()) -- reflux ratio 2.0, reboiler heat-duty spec, feed 1 mol/s 50/50 saturated liquid at stage 4, total condenser, 30s tray hydraulic time constant, 50 mol drum/sump holdup. Needs op-mp9d (public benzene()/toluene()) landed first.

physics/mod.rs: DistillationPlant struct owning a DynamicColumn + current DynamicColumnState, a PlantCommands struct (reflux_ratio, reboiler_duty_watts, feed_flow_mol_s, feed_composition -- mirror HtgrPlant::step's dt+commands signature from examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/mod.rs:723), step(dt, commands) calling DynamicColumn::step_rk4, and write_snapshot(&self, s: &mut ColumnSnapshot) populating per-stage T/x/y/L/V plus distillate/bottoms/reboiler-duty/sim_time_s scalars from DynamicColumn::profiles(&state).

Mirror examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/mod.rs's HtgrPlant::{new,step,write_snapshot} pattern exactly -- same responsibilities, same call shape, different physics backend. Start the plant from DynamicColumn::startup_state (uniform-fill, deliberately far from steady) so the transient approach to steady state is visible on launch, exactly like the validated op-6rhz test does.

V&V (per workspace mandatory rule -- methodology AND measured results in the doc comment): a test that this plant's own startup transient reaches the same steady profile op-6rhz's test independently validates, within the same tolerances (0.05 K stage temperature, 1e-4 mole fraction, 1e-3 mol/s product split).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
DONE 2026-08-15. examples/distillation_sim_v1/physics/{mod.rs,column_config.rs} built.

DistillationPlant wraps DynamicColumn + DynamicColumnState, starts from a uniform-fill startup_state (visible relaxation on launch, mirroring op-6rhz's own test), and rebuilds the DynamicColumn on an operating-point change while carrying the differential state forward unchanged (DynamicColumn bakes reflux ratio/reboiler duty in at construction with no setter -- documented in the module doc why a rebuild-on-change is both necessary and physically correct).

V&V test plant_relaxes_to_the_validated_steady_profile: measured max stage-temperature deviation 5.16e-4 K, max liquid benzene-fraction deviation 3e-6, distillate 0.499999 mol/s, bottoms 0.500001 mol/s over a 100,000 s plant-time run -- inside the pass criteria (0.05 K / 1e-4 / 1e-3 mol/s) and tighter than op-6rhz's own recorded 4e-4 K / 9.3e-6 (this run integrates much longer, ~4300 s there vs 100,000 s here, so it sits closer to true steady). Also added same_commands_are_a_no_op_rebuild confirming the rebuild-on-change logic actually advances the state rather than silently no-op'ing.

Gates: cargo test --release -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --example distillation_sim_v1 -> 3 passed, 0 failed (includes app-layer tests from op-81pb, built together).

design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


Preserve **P, S and material inventory**; solve destination-package temperature
where supported.

Appropriate for compression/expansion and state-transfer contexts.

Entropy reference conventions have the same hazard as enthalpy references, so
this depends on the reference-reconciliation work too. Not every package will
support an entropy-based solve — the capability abstraction must be able to say
so, and the error must be legible when it cannot.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Crude estimate initially**

Implement Claus SRU **as part of the refinery sulfur balance**, not as a
standalone curiosity.

Thermal stage: `2 H2S + 3 O2 -> 2 SO2 + 2 H2O`
Catalytic Claus: `2 H2S + SO2 <-> 3 S + 2 H2O`
Overall idealized: `2 H2S + O2 -> 2 S + 2 H2O`

```
acid gas -> reaction furnace -> waste-heat boiler -> sulfur condenser
         -> catalytic Claus stage -> sulfur condenser -> further stages
         -> tail gas
```

**Outputs**: elemental sulfur; steam/heat recovery; tail gas; sulfur-recovery
efficiency.

The **waste-heat boiler is a refinery heat source** and must appear in the heat
ledger.

## Hard sulfur balance

```
S in crude = S in products + elemental sulfur + S in stack/tail gas
           + S in flare + S in wastewater/sludge
```

Existing `GibbsReactor` and `EquilibriumReactor` are directly relevant to the
Claus equilibrium -- audit before writing new equilibrium code.

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: Claus sulfur recovery unit
